title: Two-address fixup pass between selection and allocation
description: x86-64 arithmetic is destructive: every three-address Lmach op becomes copy-plus-operate. Four cases, three handled inside the rule (dst=src1 drop the copy; dst=src2 commutative swap; dst=src2 integer sub becomes sub-then-neg, exact in twos complement). The fourth has no instruction-local answer: dst=src2 for subsd/divsd needs a scratch, and a rule cannot request one because the allocator runs over Lmach and never sees selected output. regs.ss now reserves rax and xmm15 as scratch so the rule HAS somewhere to put it, but the general fix is a fixup pass. RV64 will not need it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lowering pass: Lrepr to Lmach
description: GAP in the original breakdown, found while looking for the next critical-path item. E2-LIR froze the Lmach language and shipped the fixture both selectors consume, but nothing actually LOWERS Lrepr into it. Without this the pipeline has a hole between analysis and codegen and milestone 1 is unreachable no matter how good the selectors are. Flattens the expression tree into basic blocks with an explicit transfer, turns let bindings into vreg definitions carrying their storage class, turns primcalls into mach ops, and turns any check whose control is still checked or unchecked into a chk instruction while dropping the proved ones.
acceptance_criteria: nbody-inner-repr lowers to a program equal to nbody-inner-mach, and a check left as checked survives as a chk instruction while a proved one does not.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/lower.ss: Lrepr to Lmach, flattening to blocks, primcalls to mach ops, and checks resolved by control. nbody-inner-repr lowers to mul/add/load with 2 proved, 2 unchecked, 0 emitted. 12 tests.

title: No flonum negation, and (fl- 0.0 x) is not it
description: VERIFIED: (fl- 0.0 0.0) is 0.0 and (- 0.0) is -0.0, and the sign survives division: (/ (fl- 0.0 0.0) 39.47) is 0.0 while (/ (- 0.0) 39.47) is -0.0. ref.c spells offset_momentum with -px; every Scheme config we wrote spells it (fl- 0.0 px). Latent, not active: px is never exactly zero for nbody's five bodies, so the oracle passes today. But it is a real divergence from SPEC.md and a bit-exactness hazard for any future program where the momentum sum cancels. Needs a flneg primitive in lang.ss's table and SPEC.md amended to state which one is normative.
acceptance_criteria: flneg exists, the bench sources use it, SPEC.md states the normative spelling, and a test pins the zero case.
close_reason: flneg added as the normative spelling; SPEC.md states it and why (fl- 0.0 x) is not equivalent.

title: Lcore's single control input collapses D5's named granularity
description: Found by the numeric-tower agent, and it is right. lang.ss declares five named checks and a lexical policy form, but (primcall pr c e* ...) carries ONE tri-state control. So the IR can say 'bounds off in this region' at policy level and CANNOT say 'bounds unchecked, type still checked' at a call site: per-name granularity has collapsed to one bit by the time it reaches the primitive. D5 was ratified on the measurement that named granularity costs nothing (ada-8-named and ada-8-all identical at 801.00 instr/step), so this collapse discards exactly what D5 argued for. Either the control becomes a set keyed by check name, or the collapse is a documented deliberate lowering with a stated reason.
acceptance_criteria: primcall can express bounds-unchecked-but-type-checked at a single site, or LEDGER.md records why the collapse is correct.
close_reason: primcall now carries ([pn c] ...), one control per applicable check, with prim-checks declaring which apply. 'bounds elided, type still checked' is expressible and tested.

title: DECISION: does SonicScheme permit FMA contraction and reassociation?
description:
Found by the RISC-V smoke gate on day one, which is what it is for. nbody at 17 significant digits: RISC-V gcc contracts to fmadd.d by default (ONE rounding instead of two) while baseline x86-64 has no FMA to contract into, and vectorization reassociates the accumulation. Cross-ISA bit-exactness holds ONLY with contraction and vectorization both off:
  contract=fast novec  rv64 ...460623  x86 ...4606   DIFFER
  contract=off  novec  rv64 ...4606    x86 ...4606   AGREE
  contract=off  vec    rv64 ...460606  x86 ...4606   DIFFER
The oracle's nine decimals hide all of this, so METHOD.md currently passes while the underlying doubles differ. Three options: (a) forbid both, keeping bit-exact cross-ISA agreement at a real performance cost, since FMA is both faster AND more accurate; (b) permit both and make the oracle per-target with a tolerance; (c) permit contraction but not reassociation. This is a language-semantics decision, not a backend one, and it belongs in SPEC.md.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision in LEDGER.md, SPEC.md amended to state whether contraction and reassociation are permitted, and METHOD.md's oracle amended to match.
close_reason: Option (d): FP contraction is an explicit, lexically-scoped, NAMED permission, default OFF, using the same mechanism as check suppression per D5. Reassociation stays forbidden and is revisited when a real reduction benchmark enters the matrix.

title: Milestone 1: nbody compiles, runs, passes the oracle
description: The platform every later measurement is taken against. Oracle is docs/METHOD.md: energy conservation, cross-agreement to nine decimals, and the published values -0.169075164 and -0.169059907.
acceptance_criteria: nbody compiles to native code, runs, and passes all three oracle checks.

title: Differential test harness
description: MUST exist before milestone 1, not after. Compile each benchmark with all optimization disabled and again optimized, and diff the two outputs against each other. Any divergence is an unsound analysis, which is the single most dangerous failure mode in this project because a wrong abstract domain produces wrong code silently rather than failing loudly.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs both builds and diffs; deliberately breaking a transfer function is caught.
notes: CORRECTION from the RISC-V smoke gate: 'any divergence is an unsound analysis' is FALSE for floating-point once vectorization lands. Reassociation legitimately changes the result, measured at the 16th significant digit on nbody. This bead's tolerance rule depends on the FMA/reassociation decision (scheme-benchmarking-n14) and must not be implemented before it is settled.

title: Metadata emission threaded through codegen
description: PERVASIVE work and the reason D21 cannot be deferred: every backend instruction must be metadata-aware. Emit an entry before every backend instruction plus extra entries inside any instruction whose expansion changes the answer, then let the assembler dedupe. Emacs is the retrofit cost: 1842 primitives to audit, never done.
acceptance_criteria: Every backend instruction emits or inherits an entry; a synthetic multi-load sequence produces one entry per intermediate state.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/emit.ss: emit! takes bytes and metadata together so an instruction cannot be added without stating what the collector believes at it. 12 tests, including the multi-load transient window and the 100-to-1 collapse in a call-free run.

title: Object emission
description: ELF output plus the metadata blob appended after machine code and constant pool, with its size in the function header so the decoder finds it by arithmetic on the object header.
acceptance_criteria: Emitted object links and runs a trivial program on the chosen target.
close_reason: Closed

title: Register allocator enforcing the partition
description: Linear scan. Must assert that a value virtual never lands in the raw set, per E1-REGPART. This constraint is the whole reason PC-total roots need no register metadata, so a violation is a silent memory-corruption bug rather than a performance bug.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator rejects a program that would place a value virtual in a raw register; nbody's inner loop allocates with no spills on RISC-V.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/regs.ss + regalloc.ss: partition tables for both ISAs, linear scan, every assignment checked via check-assignment! which raises. 16 tests including the x86-64-spills/RV64-does-not pressure pair.

title: Instruction selection framework
description: Target-parametric. The per-target selectors plug in here. Scope to the benchmark instruction subsets, not the full ISA.
acceptance_criteria: A trivial target emits correct code for an arithmetic fixture.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/select.ss: target-parametric selection over Lmach with a per-target rule table. Coverage is a query so a port in progress reports what it owes; a missing rule raises rather than emitting nothing; a proved check reaching selection raises. 8 tests, toy target consumes the real nbody fixture.

title: Lowered machine-independent IR
description: The last IR before target divergence. Must express the register classes from E1-REGPART abstractly so selection can be written per target against one input.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures for nbody's inner loop in lowered form; both target selectors consume the same fixture.
close_reason: Lmach frozen in lang.ss; nbody-inner-mach is the fixture both target selectors consume, and it asserts no check survived to codegen.

title: PC-total metadata encoding
description: Varint step function. Per-entry: varint code offset, flag byte, second byte for multiple-values count and incoming-arguments location, signed varint pushed-values, varint layout length, packed layout bits. Frame layout is ONE function-wide bitvector computed once. The assembler drops any entry identical to its predecessor, so the table is a step function whose breakpoints are calling-convention transitions, which is why space is O(c*s/8), the same order as conventional safepoint maps.
acceptance_criteria: Encoder and decoder round-trip; a synthetic function with known transitions produces the expected entry count; lookup at an arbitrary offset returns the last entry at or before it.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/gcmeta.ss: LEB128 varints, packed frame bitvectors, per-target flag layouts, dedupe to a step function, total PC lookup. 36 tests.

title: Preemption model: no polls, restart regions
description: Per D21. No poll instruction anywhere in compiler output, no suspend flag the mutator reads, no list of allowed stopping points. Restart regions for the allocator claim-then-fill window: mark restartable and rewind the saved PC, which costs nothing on the fast path and nothing when no collection happens. Explicitly document that sonic/analyze.ss's loop primitive compiles to a jump and that this is SAFE under this model and would NOT be under a poll model.
acceptance_criteria: Written spec. A grep over emitted code for any poll or yield check returns nothing.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/preempt.ss: restart regions with overlap refused and rewind-pc; poll-free? as the executable form of the no-poll invariant, asserted against nbody's lowered inner loop with a non-vacuity control. 12 tests.

title: GC metadata vocabulary, per target from the start
description: NOT a shared enum with per-target semantics. Mezzano's extra-registers field means 'rax holds a tagged value' on x86-64 and 'x9 holds an interior pointer into x1' on arm64, so a third architecture must widen the field or accept another reinterpretation. Bundle section 8 names this as the one machine-specific part that is not mechanical and the one that will bite.
acceptance_criteria: Vocabulary defined separately per target, with a written statement of what each field means on each, and no shared field whose meaning differs.
close_reason: sonic/doc/gc-metadata.md: separate vocabularies per target. RV64 adds ra-live? (return address is an interior pointer in a register), a scratch bitmap rather than x86's nesting, and vl-live? for RVV vector-length state.

title: Inter-stage IR contracts, frozen
description: THE highest-leverage item in the project. Freezing these is what converts a depth-13 chain into a depth-4 DAG, because a pass then depends on the contract rather than on its upstream neighbour. Getting one wrong forces revision of every downstream bead, so size small and review hard.
acceptance_criteria: Every inter-stage IR has a written definition and a fixture. A pass author can construct valid input for their stage without importing any upstream pass.
close_reason: Lssa, Lrepr and Lmach added to lang.ss, each a nanopass diff against its predecessor. 25 lang tests including three construct-standalone tests and two rejection tests. A pass author can build valid input for their stage with no upstream pass in existence.

title: Register partition contract, both ISAs
description: Value, raw and dedicated classes. Per D21 the collector scavenges the value set unconditionally with NO metadata, which is what makes PC-total roots affordable. x86-64 is tight at ~7 value and ~5 raw of 15; RISC-V is comfortable at 31 GPRs. Floating-point registers are unpartitioned on both since a double can never be a tagged pointer. Dedicate registers for nil, current CPU and current thread as arm64 does (x26/x27/x28); RISC-V has no segment registers and that is the better answer anyway.
acceptance_criteria: Both partitions written down with a register-by-register table, and a checker the register allocator can assert against.
close_reason: sonic/doc/register-partition.md: RV64 14 value / 11 raw / 32 float, x86-64 8 value / 5 raw / 16 float, with structural registers named per target.

title: Core language Lcore, formalized
description: Formalize from sonic/src/sonic/analyze.ss, which already has a working A-normalized s-expression core. A-normalization is a PRECONDITION not a preference: the analysis hangs an abstract value on each variable, so an unnamed subexpression has nowhere to put its interval. Must carry primcall control inputs, declare for premises, and policy for lexical check policy.
acceptance_criteria: Grammar written; every form has a constructor, a printer and a fixture; the existing analyze.ss programs parse under it unchanged.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/lang.ss: Lcore and Lanf in nanopass. 15 lang tests pass, including four rejection tests proving the grammar refuses undeclared forms at expansion time.

title: Substrate: pass framework and identity-pass smoke test
description: boot.ss loading the framework and the passes in order. Verify with a trivial identity pass over a two-form language BEFORE writing anything real, because nanopass define-language and define-pass errors are hard to read cold and you want a known-good baseline.
acceptance_criteria: An identity pass over a two-form language round-trips a fixture unchanged.
close_reason: sonic/vendor/nanopass at bb47b56; identity pass over a two-form language round-trips a fixture unchanged under Chez 10.0.0.

title: E1: Substrate and machine model contracts
description: Blocks everything. Materially larger than a first pass suggests because D21 puts four cross-target decisions here that cannot be deferred: all four constrain the register allocator and one constrains every backend instruction. Define the machine model against BOTH ISAs here even though only one is implemented first; that is what makes RISC-V first class rather than a port. See docs/phases/07-compiler/EXECUTION.md section 4.
acceptance_criteria: Every contract has a written definition, a constructor and printer, and at least one hand-written fixture that downstream beads can use without importing an upstream pass.

title: E2: Back end
description: The serial spine, and it comes first: a compiler that emits correct scalar code is the platform every later measurement is taken against. Split by D22 into E2-core (machine independent, does NOT parallelize, treat as a chain not a swarm) and per-target selection and encoding (these DO parallelize once E2-core exists). Scope each target to the instruction subset the benchmarks need, not the full ISA.
acceptance_criteria: nbody compiles to native code and runs, on the target chosen by DEC-TGT.

title: DECISION: vendor nanopass or hand-roll the pass framework
description: CUJ.md step 1 says git submodule add nanopass-framework-scheme. Counter-evidence: sonic/ already works without it as plain R6RS libraries. Nanopass is by the Chez authors and its leverage is largest for many near-identical language definitions, which is our shape. Against: a submodule on a public repo, a build step, opaque error messages cold. Recommendation is to vendor. Nathan's call because it is a dependency decision on a public repo.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision in LEDGER.md, and either vendor/nanopass exists with the identity-pass smoke test green, or a written rationale for hand-rolling.
close_reason: Vendored as a submodule at sonic/vendor/nanopass, pinned at bb47b56. Identity-pass smoke test green under Chez 10.0.0.

title: DECISION: which target is implemented first
description: RISC-V is first class per D22, but every measured baseline in phases 3 and 4 is native x86-64 on this box, and running SonicScheme under QEMU would confound the comparison the project exists to make. Recommendation: x86-64 implemented first, BOTH machine models designed in E1. Counter-argument with real weight: implementing the second target first is the honest test of the abstraction, QEMU works, and the RV64 boot prologue is already assembled and booted in compare-operating-systems.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision in LEDGER.md naming the first target and the reason.
close_reason: x86-64 for benchmarking first (no RISC-V board yet); RISC-V smoke-tested continuously from day one via harness/smoke-riscv.sh. RISC-V performance is the higher priority once hardware exists.

title: essa does not rename tailcall operands, so every back edge is broken
description:
Found while implementing cqs.5 (loops). essa.ss's Expr transformer has no [(tailcall ,x ,x* ...) ...] clause, so nanopass's auto-generated clause copies the operands through with no env-lookup. Running essa on a letrec loop gives:

  (letrec ([loop.1 (lambda (i.2 n.3) (phi ([i.4 i.2] [n.5 n.3]) ... (tailcall loop i2 n)))]) ...)

The binders are loop.1, i2.11 and n.5; the tailcall names loop, i2 and n. The back edge therefore references variables that do not exist, and the SSA property (every use reaches its definition) does not hold on essa's output for any loop.

This is the one form stage 07 cannot do without: the back edge is where induction-variable steps and the trip count are read. loops.ss works on the contract and its fixtures are hand-written Lssa, so it is not blocked, but nothing downstream can consume essa's loop output until this is fixed.

Same omission affects (set! x e), whose target is not renamed either. Both are one clause each.
close_reason: essa.ss now has explicit tailcall, set! and declare-distinct clauses. Nanopass's generated fallthrough copied operands with no env-lookup, so every back edge named variables that did not exist. Regression test asserts the original names do not survive.

title: declare-distinct has no surface syntax, so it is unwritable from source
description: Found by the analysis-fixes agent. lang.ss has the declare-distinct production and alias.ss now consumes it correctly from hand-built Lanf, which is what its bead asked for. But expand.ss has no special form for it, so there is no path from a benchmark source to the premise. Until there is, the restrict-style non-aliasing that makes a kernel's array parameters provably distinct cannot be written by a programmer, and nbody's real entry point still gets  for everything. That is the difference between vectorizing nbody and not.
acceptance_criteria: A surface form lowers to declare-distinct, and a bench/nbody variant uses it and gets must-not from alias-query.

title: DECISION: give up the foreign-boundary property to get callee-saved raw registers on x86-64?
description:
Found by the calling-convention agent, and it correctly refused to decide it alone.

x86-64 has FOUR raw registers after scratch reservation (rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi) and ALL FOUR are caller-saved in System V. If we keep our callee-saved set inside the host's, which is what makes foreign calls cheap, there is nothing left to hold a raw word across a call. Every raw-word live range that crosses a call spills, unconditionally. RV64 has s8-s11 for exactly this and does not pay it.

Float is the same shape and worse: System V has NO callee-saved xmm at all, so any float loop containing a call spills every live double. Does not touch nbody, whose inner loop has no calls, but it touches everything else.

The lever is to declare one or two of rcx/rdx callee-saved by OUR convention and have the foreign boundary save them explicitly. That buys back raw registers across calls and makes every foreign call more expensive. It is a real trade and it is above the bead that found it.

Note this is another instance of the pattern the project keeps measuring: the design cost lands on x86-64 and not on the target we care about for performance.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision in LEDGER.md, and callconv.ss updated to match.

title: Flonum and integer constants need a literal pool. A flonum const needs
description: Flonum and integer constants need a literal pool. A flonum const needs either a pool or a second integer destination register and Lmach const gives neither, so fcvt.d.l and fmv.d.x are encodable and unreachable on RV64, and f64 abs/neg/const need a 16-byte sign mask on x86-64. Also: chk type-check names the check but not the EXPECTED TAG, so there is no constant to compare against; numeric.ss fixes a 3-bit tag and chk carries no operand saying which.

title: Return-value placement is a precoloring constraint, not an instruction
description: Return-value placement is a precoloring constraint, not an instruction. (ret v) carries no storage class, so neither selector can choose between rax and xmm0, or between a0 and fa0. Both emit a bare ret. Getting the value into the ABI return register needs the allocator to be told a vreg must land in a specific physical register, which linear scan currently cannot express.
close_reason: Closed

title: Peephole: fuse compare-and-branch. cmp-* names its result as a vreg an
description: Peephole: fuse compare-and-branch. cmp-* names its result as a vreg and branch-if is a separate instruction with anything permitted between them, so the only correct instruction-local lowering is cmp+setcc+movzx then cmp r,0 + jne. Fusing is a peephole over the selected stream, not something a per-instruction rule table can see. Both targets pay for this.

title: alias.ss is flow-insensitive because Lanf had no set!; that assumption is now stale
description: The alias agent notes it could be flow-insensitive for free because Lanf had no assignment. Lcore gained set! this session (from the expander agent's finding) and assignment conversion is a bead. The day a mutated variable can hold a reference, flow insensitivity stops being free: a variable may point at different objects at different program points. Revisit alongside the assignment-conversion bead, and alongside the widening-termination gap analyze.ss's own README already records.
close_reason: alias-analyze now refuses a program containing set!. Flow insensitivity is sound only after assignment conversion restores single assignment by boxing mutated variables; the precondition is documented in the header and enforced rather than assumed.

title: Alias analysis must consume declare-distinct
description: lang.ss now has a declare-distinct production, added because the alias agent found that declare's vocabulary was closed to check names and there was no way to assert non-aliasing. alias.ss does not yet read it. Until it does, a kernel receiving its arrays as parameters still answers may for everything, which is what nbody's real entry point looks like: the flvectors arrive as arguments and the allocation happened in a caller the compiler may not have. This is the difference between vectorizing nbody and not.
acceptance_criteria: Two parameters under declare-distinct answer must-not; without it they answer may; violating the premise is documented as undefined behaviour.
close_reason: Closed

title: Assignment conversion: box mutated variables into one-slot cells
description: Lcore now has a set! production so the expander has somewhere to put assignment, but nothing consumes it. Mutated variables must be boxed into a one-slot cell so set! becomes a store and the variable itself stays immutable, which is what SSA and the interval domain both assume. Every benchmark past config1 mutates a vector, so this is on the milestone-1 path, not optional. Note the interaction with the register partition: a boxed cell is a heap object, so the box is TAGGED even when the value inside is a raw f64, and a naive conversion would push every mutated flonum local out of the float registers and destroy the thing the project measures. Escape analysis (cqs.9) is what buys them back, so the two beads are related.
acceptance_criteria: set! on a local becomes a cell allocation plus a store; a test shows a mutated flonum local still reaching a float register when it does not escape.

title: and/or in test position must lower to nested if, not boolean temporaries
description: A front-end contract the e-SSA agent surfaced. Conjunctive tests work by NESTING: Lanf's if takes a single atom, so (and (fx<= 0 i) (fx< i n)) is already nested ifs by the time e-SSA sees it, each nested if gets its own sigma pair, and the facts compose because the inner comparison is converted under the outer edge's refined environment. Where it breaks is a test bound to a variable computed by something other than a comparison primcall: a boolean in a vector, or an and that the expander lowers to a let of a boolean rather than nested ifs. Then there is no fact to attach and the branch gets NO sigma, so the analysis goes blind at every guarded loop, which is exactly the shape config-2c and every bounds-guarded loop have.
acceptance_criteria: expand.ss lowers and/or in test position to nested if; a test pins that a guarded loop still receives sigma nodes.
notes: Related: the expander agent also found five Lcore gaps, four now fixed (void, set!, letrec*, top-level Program). The fifth, rest parameters, is refused loudly rather than silently lowered.
close_reason: Closed

title: phi names the merge but not per-predecessor operands
description: From the e-SSA agent's design audit. Lanf's if is not a SimpleExpr, so a diamond has no syntactic point where the arms' values meet and flow onward. Consequence: real phis are loop headers (a letrec-bound lambda's parameters ARE the phis) and value-position diamonds named where produced, as (phi ([join (if ...)]) join). That second form is a phi in POSITION rather than in operand structure: it names the merge but not the per-arm incoming values. If ABCD wants per-predecessor operands for its constraint graph, the frozen phi production cannot carry them and needs either (phi ([x e* ...] ...) body) or a join-continuation lowering. Decide BEFORE cqs.2 (ABCD) starts, since ABCD is the consumer.
acceptance_criteria: Either phi carries per-predecessor operands, or LEDGER.md records why position-only suffices for ABCD.
close_reason: phi now carries per-predecessor operands: (phi ([x (pred val) ...] ...) body). Header phis label the entry edge, which is what ABCD needs. Value-position diamonds keep one join-labelled operand, documented, because Lanf's if is not a SimpleExpr and naming the arms needs a join-continuation lowering.

title: sigma cannot express a NEGATED comparison, so flonum false edges are lost
description: Found by the e-SSA agent, which refused to emit the unsound thing rather than working around it. On the false edge of (fl< a b) we know (not (fl< a b)). That is NOT (fl>= a b), because NaN makes every comparison false, so the negation is true for NaN while fl>= is false. Emitting a fl>= sigma there asserts an ordering in exactly the case where no ordering holds, and the consumer is bounds-check elision, so it is a wrong-code bug rather than a precision loss. Current state is SOUND: the agent emits flonum sigma on the true edge only, where swapping is valid because both spellings are false for NaN. Fix is a negation flag on the sigma production, (sigma x0 x1 pr x2 negated? body), so sigma records the SYNTACTIC fact and the domain decides what it can conclude per type: for fixnums not(a<b) implies a>=b, for flonums it implies nothing without a non-NaN premise. Preferred over adding flnlt-style primitives because it generalises to every comparison and keeps the table small.
acceptance_criteria: sigma carries negation; flonum false edges are emitted; the interval domain refuses to refine a negated flonum comparison without a non-NaN premise, with a test that pins the NaN case.
close_reason: Closed

title: No type predicates in the primitive table, so config-2c is inexpressible
description: No flvector?, vector?, fixnum?, flonum?, and no error. Concrete consequence: configuration 2c is DEFINED by its predicate guards, so it cannot be written in Lcore, and phase 3's finding that predicate guards recover nothing cannot be reproduced through our own compiler. If declare premises are meant to replace predicates, that substitution must be written down, because it changes what config-2c means.
acceptance_criteria: Either the predicates and error are in the table, or LEDGER.md records the premise-for-predicate substitution and what it does to config-2c.
close_reason: fixnum?, flonum?, vector?, flvector? and error added, so config-2c's predicate guards are expressible in Lcore.

title: Keep the RISC-V smoke gate green as work lands
description: harness/smoke-riscv.sh runs cross-compile plus user-mode QEMU with no root. It is a CORRECTNESS and AVAILABILITY gate, never a performance one: QEMU timing is meaningless and every number stays x86-64 until a board exists. Extend it as SonicScheme grows: today it checks gcc's output, and once the compiler emits RV64 it asserts on our own disassembly. Toolchain is riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc 15.2.0, qemu-system-riscv64 10.2.1, and qemu-user extracted to ~/.local/opt/qemu-user.
acceptance_criteria: smoke-riscv.sh passes on every commit that touches the compiler, and any new dependency is checked for RISC-V availability before it is adopted.

title: Fixpoint analyzer over the core language
description: Walks a core-language program threading an environment of intervals, refines on comparisons, runs loops to a fixpoint with widening, and reports one elision verdict per vector reference.
acceptance_criteria: Eliminates nbody's b[i*7+k] against a length-35 vector and correctly refuses on unknown length, negative-capable index, upper-guard-only and overrunning derived index.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/analyze.ss, 11 cases passing

title: Interval abstract domain
description: Level 2 Cousot domain: exact integer bounds with neginf/posinf, join, meet, transfer functions, widening and narrowing, refinement from comparisons, iv-within? as the elision query. Built standalone before any compiler existed, which is the pattern EXECUTION.md section 1 rests on.
acceptance_criteria: Exhaustive soundness by concretization over [-4,4]^2 for add, sub and mul, plus widening direction and termination tests.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/interval.ss, 6101 checks passing

title: Bump allocator with restart regions
description: Sufficient through milestone 5 on its own, because nbody allocates almost nothing. Restart regions cover the claim-then-fill window where memory is not yet a valid object: mark restartable and rewind the saved PC. Wait-free, and the thread does not poll, cooperate, or know it happened.
acceptance_criteria: Allocation fast path is a pointer bump; an interrupt inside the fill window is restarted correctly in a test.
close_reason: Closed

title: Calling convention

title: Milestone 3: beat tuned scalar SBCL

title: Disassembly assertions
description: Milestones are verified in emitted code, not by timing. These are greps over our own disassembler output and should be tests rather than observations.

title: RVV emission, length agnostic
description: NOT the same problem as AVX-512. RISC-V Vector is length agnostic: vector length is a runtime value the loop reads via vsetvli and adapts to, so the loop structure differs and the tail handling that AVX-512 needs mostly disappears.
acceptance_criteria: Packed f64 arithmetic in nbody's inner loop under QEMU, verified in disassembly, with correct results for a vector length the loop did not know at compile time.
notes: OPEN QUESTION from E1-GCVOCAB: vsetvl establishes vector length and element width as live machine state across instructions. If preemption lands mid-loop and the restart path does not restore it, the loop resumes at a different vector length and silently computes a wrong answer. Whether restart regions extend to a vsetvl-established context, or vector loops need their own restart discipline, depends on how E5 structures its loops. Decide here, not in E1.

title: Alias analysis
description: Required for vectorization legality: the arrays must be provably distinct.
acceptance_criteria: Distinguishes two provably disjoint flvectors and refuses on a may-alias fixture.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/alias.ss: flow-insensitive, allocation-site points-to over Lanf. Distinguishes two disjoint make-flvector sites (must-not) and refuses on every may-alias fixture: same variable against itself, escape through an unknown call, two names for one base, storage into a heap object, capture by an escaping closure, a reference returned by an opaque call. Soundness direction is the opposite of the interval domain's and is stated in the header: may is the safe answer, every default and every unhandled form lands there, must-not is only returned from a positive proof. Interprocedural step propagates actuals into the formals of a KNOWN procedure (bound once, to a lambda, used only as a call operator), which is what cqs.8 raises. 14 cases, 0 failures.

title: Loop recognition, induction variables, trip count
description: Gates E5's unroll factor, not just check hoisting: Larsen's applu goes from 22.56 percent vectorizable at 256 bits to 0.01 percent at 1024 when a vectorizer guesses a trip count. Also note Clousot validates 88.9 percent of array accesses with NO loop pass at all, so this buys hoisting rather than provability and can be thinner than the pipeline ordering suggests.
acceptance_criteria: Trip counts recovered for nbody's three loops; natural loops identified in an irreducible-CFG fixture.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/loops.ss + test/loops-test.ss, 57 checks green. Natural loops as SCCs over the letrec call graph (irreducible cycles named, not forced into a header shape); basic IVs from back-edge steps, derived IVs as affine forms; trip counts exact/bound/unknown with a reason, exact only under a single back edge and a single distinct IV guard. nbody's three loops: bodies exact 5, fields exact 7, the triangular pairs loop bounded [0,4] and NOT exact. b[i*7+k] recovered as a derived IV with span exactly [0,34]. Found and filed cqs.17: essa emits back edges whose operands were never renamed.

acceptance_criteria: nbody's inner loop keeps all doubles unboxed in FP registers across the loop body.

GATE NOT RESULT: ABCD removed 45 percent of bounds checks for about 10 percent speedup because Jalapeno had no global code motion to consume the freedom. Removing a check is worth something only if a later pass uses the freedom, and our consumer is E5.

Unique names per definition, phi at loop headers (letrec-bound lambda parameters) and at value-position diamond joins, sigma on both edges of comparison branches over the constrained variables only. 34 structural assertions in sonic/test/essa-test.ss, 0 failures. Two Lssa adequacy findings reported to the epic owner: no false-edge sigma is expressible for fx= (no disequality primitive) or for any flonum comparison (NaN breaks negation), and a conjunctive test cannot be split at all since Lanf gives the if a single atom.

acceptance_criteria: Output has no nested non-atomic operands; existing analyze.ss fixtures are reproduced.

D5 is ratified on measurement, ada-8-named and ada-8-all being identical to the instruction at 801.00, so granularity is free. Unlike Chez's optimize-level this must be a lexical form, which is wall 3 of the four that made Chez unable to host the experiment.
acceptance_criteria: A policy form suppresses a named check inside its scope and not outside it, verified in emitted code.

title: Fixture vocabulary and printers
description: Constructors and a printer per IR so every downstream bead writes test inputs without importing an upstream pass. This is the bead that keeps the DAG wide; without it every pass secretly depends on its predecessor.
acceptance_criteria: For each IR, a fixture module that constructs and prints valid instances, used by at least one test in another epic.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/fixtures.ss: straight-line/diamond/loop shapes plus nbody's inner loop at Lanf, Lssa, Lrepr and Lmach. 8 tests.

title: Redefinition cell and seal bit
description: A pointer store into a data slot, NEVER a patched branch. FENCE.I is optional (Zifencei) and local-hart only, so cross-hart instruction visibility needs a data fence plus an IPI to every remote hart. Mezzano's arm64 port already declines patching, with both activation functions literal no-ops, and its x86-64 patching path carries three FIXMEs for locking, fences and cross-CPU. The seal bit lives in that same cell: sealed means the compiler may inline through it.
acceptance_criteria: Cell layout written; redefinition is a single store; a sealed cell permits inlining and an unsealed one does not, both covered by tests.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/gcell.ss: redefinition is a store into a stable cell, never a patched branch; seal bit in the same cell licenses inlining and is one-way and enforced. 9 tests.

title: E6: Verification and milestones
description: Not a phase at the end. Each milestone closes by the epic that reaches it, and the differential harness must exist BEFORE milestone 1. Differential testing is the load-bearing part: compile with all optimization disabled, diff against optimized, any divergence is an unsound analysis.
acceptance_criteria: All six milestones from CUJ.md closed, each by its stated check.

title: E4: Analysis
description: The widest epic and where swarm width lives, because every pass here is testable on fixtures alone. Partly done already: the interval domain and the fixpoint analyzer exist and pass 6101 and 11 checks. Internal edges are real but shallow.
acceptance_criteria: Each pass has fixture tests, and the elision pass removes the bounds check from nbody's inner loop as verified in disassembly.

title: E3: Front end
description: Reader, syntax-rules expander, surface to core, declaration forms, A-normalization. Deliberately NOT first: a reader is a solved problem with no research risk, and starting here spends weeks before learning anything. On the milestone-1 path, not on the risk path, so it runs alongside E2.
acceptance_criteria: bench/nbody source in SonicScheme surface syntax reaches the core language and matches a hand-written core fixture.

title: No non-NaN premise, so negated flonum comparisons can never refine
description: The NaN fix is correct and deliberately incomplete. iv-refine now declines to narrow on a NEGATED flonum comparison, because (not (fl< a b)) is true for NaN while (fl>= a b) is false. Verified: fixnum negated < gives [0,+inf], flonum negated < stays [-inf,+inf]. The agent did NOT invent a non-NaN premise mechanism, correctly, since no production carries one and inventing vocabulary would have been a second decision inside a soundness fix. The consequence is that a float loop guarded by a negated comparison gets no refinement at all on the false edge, forever, until such a premise exists. Candidates: a declare premise naming non-NaN, or deriving it from a preceding (fl= x x) test, which is the standard idiom.
acceptance_criteria: A non-NaN premise exists; a negated flonum comparison refines under it and still refuses without it.
close_reason: premise vocabulary split from policy vocabulary; non-nan added; iv-edge-cmp and iv-refine take an optional non-nan? that unlocks negated flonum comparisons. Defaults to #f so the safe answer is free. 6117 interval checks.

title: Chez does not promise left-to-right evaluation for map or let bindings
description: A trap the calling-convention agent hit twice while writing ordered passes with mutable side tables. Chez evaluates let bindings and map's applications in unspecified order, so a stateful counter threaded through either produces a different answer between runs or between optimize levels. Both instances are fixed in callconv.ss, but the same trap will bite anyone writing an ordered pass over this tree, and several passes do exactly that. Worth a note in the contributor docs and worth grepping for.
acceptance_criteria: A note in sonic/README.md, and a grep over the tree for map/let used with a mutable counter.
close_reason: essa.ss defines map/lr and uses it at all six (map fresh-name ...) sites; determinism verified by compiling the same program twice and comparing. Documented in sonic/README.md.

title: selector-covers? reports rules that raise as covered. It checks rule P
description: selector-covers? reports rules that raise as covered. It checks rule PRESENCE, not success, so a target that has a rule which immediately errors looks complete. Both agents deliberately used raising rules for the things they could not implement, which is honest, but coverage then overstates readiness.
close_reason: selector-owed lets a target declare what it cannot do yet, and missing-rules counts those as missing. Rule presence no longer implies readiness.

title: div-check is declared but unreachable; comparison sets asymmetric; arity unspecified
description: Three smaller table defects from the same review. (1) div-check has nothing to attach to: no fx/, fxquotient, fxremainder, fxmodulo, and fl/ by zero is an IEEE infinity rather than an error, so trapping it would make the C arm right and us wrong. Add integer division or drop the check name. (2) Fixnums get five comparisons, flonums three; no fl> or fl>=. NaN makes fl> genuinely NOT derivable from fl<= by negation, so this bites harder for flonums. (3) (primcall pr c e* ...) admits any operand count. For flonums the association order of a multi-operand form is observable in the result bits, so the expander must fix it and the runtime must not. An unfilled make-vector is also a wild pointer under a scanning collector.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three is either fixed in the table or has a written rationale.
close_reason: div-check made reachable via fxquotient/fxremainder/fxmodulo (fl/ deliberately excluded, IEEE says infinity); fl> and fl>= added since NaN makes them underivable from fl<=; arity stated per primitive with mandatory fill on make-vector/make-flvector.

title: Alias the allocation check with remembered-set overflow
description: Allocation pointer grows UP from the nursery base, remembered-set pointer grows DOWN from its top. Running out of nursery and running out of remembered-set space become the same event on the same path, so the store buffer's dedicated limit register and its bound check are both free.
acceptance_criteria: One comparison triggers both conditions; a test drives each to its limit independently.

title: Write barrier, Chez-style, no generation check
description: Store, test one tag bit on the value, push the slot address if not a fixnum. The mutator NEVER reads the segment table; all filtering is deferred and batched. About ten instructions per pointer store. Chez's own collector comment records that the older-than test was measured and rejected as not worth the memory reads. Note the barrier is the price of choosing GENERATIONS, not of mutation: Loko, Gambit and Guile all have full mutation and no barrier because none is generational.
acceptance_criteria: Barrier is at most about ten instructions in emitted code; a cross-generation store is caught.

title: Primitives
description: The primitive set the benchmarks need, with control inputs per Lcore's primcall.
acceptance_criteria: Every primitive used by bench/nbody has an implementation and a test.
close_reason: Primitives landed in sonic/src/sonic/prims.ss. All 33 primitives from the frozen table in lang.ss and nothing else, as a data table keyed by symbol with the control input as an argument, matching Lcore's (primcall pr c e* ...). checked runs the named check and signals a sonic-condition carrying the check name, who, and irritants; unchecked and proved emit identical code, and only proved is auditable. Bounds, type and overflow checks are separately named so they can be counted by name per D5. prims.ss deliberately does not import (sonic lang) to keep the runtime independent of the compiler's IR library; the two tables are cross-checked in both directions by the test. Every primitive nbody uses is covered, plus an end-to-end b[i*7+k] kernel asserted bit-identical under all three controls. Test: cd sonic && scheme -q --libdirs src:vendor/nanopass --script test/numeric-test.ss -> 324 checks, 0 failures.

title: Precise generational copying collector
description: NOT Boehm. RESEARCH.md section 3 shows Boehm is exactly where Stalin loses 5x to 16x on allocation-heavy code. Two generations, bump allocation in the nursery, Cheney scan, precise roots from E2-META's stack maps. No shadow stack is needed because we own the frame layout.
acceptance_criteria: Collects a fixture heap correctly; precise roots verified by a test that would leak or crash under conservative scanning.
notes: Collector is a Scheme library that emits instruction lists at compile time, not a C program linked in. See E7 notes.

title: Numeric tower: fixnum and flonum only
description: No bignum, ratnum or complex initially. The benchmarks need none, and the tower is where a naive implementation loses all its performance.
acceptance_criteria: Fixnum overflow and flonum edge cases behave per R7RS for the supported subset.
close_reason: Numeric tower landed in sonic/src/sonic/numeric.ss. Fixnum and flonum only, no bignum/ratnum/complex. Tag scheme: 3 tag bits, fixnum tag 000, 64-bit word, so 61 value bits and range [-2^60, 2^60-1] = [-1152921504606846976, 1152921504606846975], which is what CUJ.md stage 8 already assumed and is also Chez's width so the hosted model shares the host's overflow boundary. Overflow documented and tested under all three controls: checked signals overflow-check with no bignum promotion; unchecked is UB and wraps two's-complement mod 2^61 with the tag surviving; proved emits unchecked code and is auditable via proved-audit, which accuses the analysis rather than the program. Flonums are IEEE binary64, one correctly rounded op per primitive, contraction never applied per D24, with a witness triple in the suite where one rounding and two differ by ~1.9x. 324 checks, 0 failures.

title: Milestone 5: beat gcc -O3 -march=native
description: Phase 3 measured c-native at 333.00 instr/step and 33.92 ns/step, 0.91x c-scalar. The instruction-count target is aggressive; the wall-clock target is closer than it looks because nbody is latency bound.
acceptance_criteria: bench.sh shows SonicScheme at or ahead of c-native with a bootstrap CI excluding 1.0.

title: Milestone 4: packed arithmetic in the inner loop
description: Verified in disassembly on both targets.
acceptance_criteria: E6-DISASM packed-arithmetic assertion passes on x86-64 and RV64.

title: AVX-512 emission
description: Fixed width. Target vfmadd231pd on zmm registers for an f64 loop. Note phase 3 measured c-native at 0.51x the instruction count of c-scalar but only 0.91x the wall time, because nbody is latency bound on a sqrt dependency chain, so expect about 2x in work and about 1.1x in time on THIS program.
acceptance_criteria: vfmadd231pd on a zmm register appears in nbody's inner loop, verified in disassembly.

title: Vectorization legality
description: Shared by both targets. Needs the trip count from E4-LOOP, distinctness from E4-ALIAS, unboxed storage from E4-REPR, and the checks gone from E4-ELIDE since a bounds check in the loop body makes vectorization illegal.
acceptance_criteria: Correctly permits nbody's inner loop and refuses a loop with a loop-carried dependence.

title: Procedure inlining
description: CARRY THIS NUMBER: nbody is the one benchmark where Chez's cp0 inliner does NOT help, 0.92 to 1.05 on the R4400 per Waddell and Dybvig, attributed to cache effects from three-level nested array indexing without measuring that attribution. A pass showing nothing on nbody is the EXPECTED result, not a bug. Note also that aggressive inlining removes call sites, which under a poll-based preemption model would remove safepoints; under D21 that is a non-issue, which is one more argument for D21.
acceptance_criteria: Inlines a leaf call in a fixture; measured effect on nbody is reported, not required to be positive.
close_reason: sonic/src/sonic/inline.ss: Lanf -> Lanf. Inlines a leaf call in the fixture. Five rules: known callee, size budget 12 Lanf nodes, not on the active inline stack (this is the termination proof, kept separate from the recursion rule so relaxing that one cannot make the pass diverge), not self- or mutually-recursive, and at non-tail sites exactly one tail position so the continuation is spliced rather than copied into every branch. Effects cannot be duplicated: Lanf operands are atoms, so a parameter is substituted by a variable, never by the expression that produced it. ANF invariant checked in the test by an independent walker (result still named at the call's binding, binders unique, no free variable introduced). nbody effect NOT measured and not claimed: nothing here is tuned toward it, per Waddell and Dybvig's 0.92-1.05 on the R4400. Demonstrated payoff is on cqs.7 instead: a helper called on two array pairs merges its formals and alias says may; inline it and each site's arrays are provably distinct. 21 checks, 0 failures.

title: Escape analysis
description: Enables stack allocation. One of the four places PLAN.md identifies where we would exceed SBCL, since CL's dynamic-extent is manual.
acceptance_criteria: A non-escaping allocation is stack-allocated in a fixture; an escaping one is not.

title: Pentagon domain
description: Level 3: x in [a,b] AND x < y. Per D6 do NOT add closure: it made Pentagons LESS precise on three of four .NET assemblies (82.77 vs 83.19 on mscorlib) while tripling analysis time, and Pentagon's Sub having no closure is what makes Mine's infinite-chain widening hazard structurally impossible. Watch Figure 3, which prints an unsound widening in both halves, masked whenever iterates increase monotonically.
acceptance_criteria: Soundness by exhaustive concretization as interval-test.ss does, plus explicit widening-direction tests.

title: syntax-rules expander
description: Enough for the declaration forms and the benchmark programs. Not full syntax-case.
acceptance_criteria: Expands the benchmark macros and a hygiene torture fixture correctly.
close_reason: syntax-rules expander landed in sonic/src/sonic/expand.ss with sonic/test/expand-test.ss. 133 checks, 0 failures. Literals by denotation, pattern variables, nested ellipsis with (... ...) escape and multi-ellipsis splicing, improper patterns, vector patterns, custom ellipsis identifier, let-syntax/letrec-syntax. Hygiene by binder alpha-renaming plus per-expansion template aliasing into the macro's definition environment; both capture directions covered by the or/swap! torture fixtures plus nested-ellipsis cases. Derived forms let*, named let, when, unless, cond (with else and =>), and, or, begin, one-armed if and internal defines all reduced to Lcore shapes. Acceptance: all six bench/nbody Scheme sources expand with no derived form surviving, and the five Chez-runnable ones compute the same energy as the original under Chez's own expander.

title: Surface to core
description: Surface syntax down to Lcore.
acceptance_criteria: bench/nbody surface source parses to a core form matching a hand-written fixture.

title: Reader
description: Datum syntax. Solved problem, no research risk, which is why this epic is not first.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trips every datum in bench/nbody sources.
close_reason: (sonic read) lands an R7RS datum reader; test/read-test.ss is 132 checks, 0 failures, and its core is a differential round-trip of all six bench/nbody Scheme sources against Chez's own read, datum by datum plus every flonum through number->string, with 27 negative cases so the reader refuses malformed input.

title: E7: Runtime
description: Fully parallel, can start as soon as E1 fixes the stack-map and partition contracts, and absorbs slack for anyone blocked. A bump allocator that never collects suffices through milestone 5 because nbody allocates almost nothing, so the GC bead is real but low urgency. Four mechanisms to copy outright rather than invent, all from the compare-operating-systems bundle.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime test suite green with NO C in the running system, and nbody runs to completion under the real allocator.
notes: CORRECTED: the runtime is Scheme, not C. Per compare-operating-systems lessons/metacircular-bootstrap.md, Loko's collector is a Scheme library emitting instruction lists at COMPILE time, so at run time there is only a label in the text segment. What must be written in something else is ~60 straight-line instructions that discover nothing, and we emit those ourselves. A C runtime would drag a C toolchain and libc into a kernel written in Scheme, which is what CIVICS exists not to be. Licensing: Loko is copyleft; take the shape from the description, do not copy code. Read Mezzano (MIT) and Chez (Apache 2.0) for detail.

title: E5: Vectorization
description: The headline capability and genuinely last. No Lisp-family compiler auto-vectorizes: Chez emits only scalar sd forms, SBCL can encode AVX-512 but has no vectorization pass, sb-simd stops at AVX2. The two targets are NOT the same problem: AVX-512 is fixed width, RVV is length agnostic with vector length a runtime value the loop adapts to. Two beads sharing one legality analysis, not one bead with a flag.
acceptance_criteria: Packed arithmetic in nbody's inner loop, verified in disassembly, on both targets.

title: Lanf has no Prog nonterminal, so opaque externals are spelled as typos
description: From the alias agent. Lmach has a Prog production and Lanf does not, so 'opaque, outside this compilation unit' has to be spelled as an unbound free variable in operator position. It works and it is indistinguishable from a misspelling, which means a genuine typo reads as a deliberate external reference and gets the conservative answer instead of an error. Lcore gained a top-level Program production this session; Lanf and Lssa should carry it through.
close_reason: Lcore's Program production now carries an explicit extern list, inherited by Lanf and Lssa. An unbound variable is a bug again rather than being indistinguishable from a deliberate opaque reference.

title: Reserve the collection worst case up front
description: The only systems in the OS bundle that survive heap exhaustion do this: Loko lifts a 128KB margin, Mezzano subtracts the memory required for collection from free store before any expansion, Biscuit combines a static per-entry-point bound with per-processor reservation credit. Linux, Chez and Mirage all die instead, and Mirage does not even have an exit code for it.
acceptance_criteria: Heap exhaustion under test returns a Scheme-level condition rather than aborting.

title: Constant per-byte GC assist
description: A fixed tax from day one, NOT a proportional feedback pacer. Biscuit deleted Go's proportional assist computation and replaced it with a constant, because a control loop has transients and an unbounded assist charge can land inside a lock or an interrupt handler.
acceptance_criteria: Assist charge is a constant function of bytes allocated, with no feedback term anywhere.

title: Milestone 6: Pentagon and loops carry fannkuchredux
description: Requires fannkuchredux written first under the bench/nbody/SPEC.md discipline, which does not exist yet.
acceptance_criteria: fannkuchredux passes its oracle and its bounds checks are elided.
